root_cause: U10 sits inside the /SENSEC2 high-current corridor band [32.5,48.1,9.5,27.5], fragmenting both /SENSEC2_HI (2 islands, 6 foreign crossings) and /SENSEC2_LO (2 islands, 17 foreign crossings). The fragmented pours drive the 14 structural DRC violations (island boundary clearance conflicts with foreign copper cuts) and the 4 conductor-over-temp FEM flags on GND and the two SENSEC2 nets (thermal load concentrates at the constriction between islands). The 2 unconnected stubs (/DETC1, /DETC2) are secondary — detection signal nets that cannot complete routing across the congested fragmented corridor. More router effort cannot fix island fragmentation caused by a body occupying the pour band; this is a placement fault requiring eviction of U10 outside the /SENSEC2 corridor before routing re-runs.
reasoning: SENSEC1 nets (single island each, fewer foreign crossings) are intact and passing pour-integrity. SENSEC2 nets are the only clipped pair, and the deterministic body-in-corridor check identifies U10 as the sole body inside that band. Kelvin gates pass (kelvin_unrouted=0), so the sense topology is correct — the problem is purely the foreign body fragmenting the pour, not a routing quality issue. Evicting U10 clears the corridor, allows a single-island pour on SENSEC2_HI and SENSEC2_LO, eliminates the thermal constrictions, and removes the DRC-triggering island boundaries. The /DETC1 and /DETC2 stubs will likely close once corridor congestion is resolved. No scorer reweight is appropriate — no gate-passing candidate exists to rank.

proposed_lever.detail: Evict U10 and its owned passive cluster out of the /SENSEC2 band [32.5,48.1,9.5,27.5]. Relocate to a region outside both SENSEC cable corridors (e.g. the logic/control zone right of the ESP or above SENSEC1 band) preserving decoupling cap adjacency. Do not move shunts RS* or connectors J*. After eviction re-run bake_hints keepouts to enforce the cleared corridor before the next FR pass.
